characters.description: Glowing Eyes of Doom: His eyes are shown gleaming white in Sir Pentious's flashback. Karma Houdini: Since Sir Pentious never reported him, he faced no consequences (at least, no earthly ones) and killed five more women. No Name Given: Sir Pentious knows he was a wealthy and powerful individual but his specific name isn't given. That said, it's heavily implied that he'sbased onthe historicJack the Ripper, given that he was active in London during the 1880s, murdered exclusively women and was never caught. Screw the Rules, I Have Money!: He is stated to be a rich and powerful individual that also happens to be Sir Pentious' client. Pentious' reluctance of reporting him to the authorities was likely due to fear of retribution from offending a man of such wealth and influence. Small Role, Big Impact: Sir Pentious believes that him not reporting the killer's identity out of cowardice was what damned him to Hell, and by proxyallowed him to be the first sinner to redeem himself and enter Heaven.

characters.name: Alastor's Victim
characters.description: Seen in "It's a Deal". A high society type in New Orleans whom Alastor murdered after he had spilled wine on the future Radio Demon's sleeve. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear if he spilled wine on Alastor's suit on purpose or if it was a genuine accident. Similarly, it's unclear if his laughter is because he's anUpper-Class TwitJerkassor a racist. Asshole Victim: Whilehis murder is horrific, and it's ambiguous whether the first time he stains Alastor is on purpose or by accident, the way he laughs at Alastor after realizing he did it and thenkeepsspilling his drink on him does not endear him to any viewers for the few seconds he's onscreen and no one in the audience mourns him. Casting Gag:Brandon Rogersis best known for voicinga professional hitmanwithin the Hellaverse, so having him also voice a murder victim (who is in line withthe hitman's usual kinds of targets, no less) makes for some irony. Death by Racism: It's strongly implied that he did himself in because of him spilling some wine on Alastor while at a party; considering the time period he did so, causing trouble to Alastor intentionally because of him being mixed race, it's safe to assume what lead to Alastor murdering him.

characters.name: Alastor's Killer
characters.description: Accidental Hero: Sure, his shooting of Alastor wasAccidental Murder, but hedidend up stopping a cannibalisticSerial Killerfrom continuing his spree.In life at least. Accidental Murder: As stated above, the hunter killing Alastor was due to mistaking him for a deer while he was dragging a body through the woods at night. Ambiguous Situation: Alastor died the day aftermaking a deal with Rosie.Rosieherself not only knew, but rubbed the coincidence in Alastor's face, hinting that this may have in fact been by her design. Boom, Headshot!: How he killed Alastor, mistaking him for his prey, via scope. The Faceless: His face is not shown, and he's only seen from waist down.

characters.name: Vincent's Victims
characters.description: Seen in "Brighter" from "Weapon of Mass Distraction". Various television presenters of a station whom Vincent Whittman (later Vox) had murdered so he could ascend the media ladder. They include a news anchor, a late-night talk show host, a pair of producers, a zoo show host, a cooking show hostess, a game show host, and the network's CEO, Robert "Bob" Sinclaire. Bludgeoned to Death: Vincent killed the talk show host by repeatedly bashing one of the talk show's set lamps on him. Cruel and Unusual Death: Most of Vincent's kills were brutal, but the ones that particularly take the cake are those of the producers (both strangled and then hanged from a microphone cord) and Bob (thrown off the network buildingafterbeing stabbed andwhileelectrocuted by lightning). Desecrating the Dead: Vincent not only killed the news anchor to take his job, he also danced with his corpse and left it in a dumpster in an alleyway. Harmful to Minors: At least one little girl was present and witnessed Bob's charred corpse hit the pavement.

characters.name: Eve
characters.description: Did They or Didn't They?: Lucifer's comments in the Season 1 finale seem to imply that he not only married Lilith, he may have also seduced Eve at some point as well. Though it's not clear if he's merely mocking theOriginal Manor not, and it's also possible he was simply referring tooffering Eve the Forbidden Fruit. Given that Adam is aPsychopathic ManchildandPolitically Incorrect Villain, andhas been since the dawn of creation,can you really blame her if she did? Missing Mom: She's essentially the "Mother of Humanity", but hasn't made an appearance. Second Love: Was this to Adam after Lilith ditched him for being controlling. Slasher Smile: In Charlie's story, after Eve takes the Fruit of Knowledge, she's shown sporting aPsychotic Smirkthat grows into a terrifying red-tinted smile—possibly implying that either given freedom had corrupted her, or there was already something wrong with her before eating the fruit. Small Role, Big Impact: Her current role is in a flashback in a story Charlie told. However, her eating the fruit allowed evil to enter Earth and cause Lucifer's banishment to Hell.

characters.name: Hell and Demons in general

Sinners have a wide range of blood colors, like pink for Angel Dust. Imps and other Hellborn demons are shown to have black blood inHelluva Boss. Always Chaotic Evil:Downplayed. Sinner demons don't turn more evil once they end up in Hell, but due to the fact the overwhelming majority among them are therebecausethey were terrible people in life, it'slargely a self-reinforcing pit of misery, and even the demons who want to be redeemed note thatthey feel they're in too deep to be successfully redeemed(like Angel Dust). Hell only encourages their worst character traits as a result, withdemonkind commonly regarding virtue as a weakness, leading to the demons that aren't evil or just straight-up jerks being counted down on one hand (Charlie, Vaggie, Mrs. Mayberry and Beelzebub along with a handful of others on a good day). AlsoDeconstructed- the prologue implies that Heaven views them this way becausethey dared to go against God's plan, with the continuous oppression resulting in a case ofThen Let Me Be Evil. This is made worse by the fact that, as revealed in "Welcome in Heaven",the system determining whether a soul goes to Heaven or Hell is completely opaque to everyone, Heaven included, so without being able to actually know what qualifies a soul being able to enter Heaven is like winning a metaphorical lottery. Angels assume that whoever goes in Heaven or Hell must deserve it, regardless of their behavior in their past or afterlife. This is later subverted in Season 2, since many Sinners are shown checking into the hotel in search of redemption, showing that although there are bad Sinners, many of them are willing to change for the better once proof of redemption being possible is shown. characters.name: In General
characters.description: 15 Minutes of Fame: Theirmodus operandifor employed talent is to overexpose them until everybody gets sick of it (enough that they cannot even profit from hate views), knowing that there's always more idiots out there to exploit. Unless they're a ridiculously popular superstar like Angel Dust or Katie Killjoy, no Sinner's lasting long. Alphabetical Theme Naming: All three of their names start with the letter "V", and that's why they're called the Vees. Allegorical Character: While each of them represents a type of modern media, the Vees collectively represent its worst aspects, namely how they recruit and groom up-and-coming talent with promises of money and fame, only to ruthlessly exploit them with little regard for their physical or mental well-being and toss them out the moment they're no longer marketable.Vox represents television, owning several shows and businesses, and quite literally hypnotizing viewers.Velvette represents social media, constantly being on her phone to keep up with the latest trends and fashion. characters.name: Lilith
characters.description: The Queen of Hell and Charlie's mother, she is the one who defied Adam's authority and escaped the Garden of Eden. After encountering Lucifer, she became his wife and co-architect in the accidental dooming of humanity and the creation of Hell. She has been absent from the royal family for seven years. Ambiguously Evil: While Charlie has nothing but good things to say about her, theofficial trading card of her◊that was part of a pre-release promotion portrays her in a mysterious, somewhat sinister light.In the season 1 finale, we learn that she's been in Heaven this whole time, thanks to a deal she apparently made with Adam, with the newly empowered Lute demanding that she do something about her daughter. What this means regarding her relationship with her family and with the angels is hard to say, though itdefinitelymakes her seem like a shitty parent who was too busy enjoying a vacation to bother responding to her daughter's calls for emotional support. On the other hand, Lilith is never shown to be happy in Heaven andwhile she declines Charlie's calls without changing expression, the way she lingers on it and her other unanswered messages from Charlie and Lucifer implies that she's more affected than she lets on.. Ambiguously Human: AmbiguouslySinner. While it’s confirmed she was the original first woman, it’s not clear what exactly she is in present. While she is in Hell, Charlie’s story (if taken at face value) indicates that she was banished there alongside Lucifer rather than dying and being sent there. This, alongside the fact that she and Lucifer were able to have Charlie when Sinners are unable to have children, plus her rather human-like appearance and the fact that from what we know, she didn’t eat the Fruit of Knowledge that resulted in mankind’s ability to sin, makes her current status ambiguous. characters.name: Susan
characters.description: The hardest cannibal to impress in all of Cannibal Town. Evil Old Folks: She's old and a member of the cannibal town, and is overall a rude and unpleasant person as opposed to the moreAffably Evilmembers of the town. The Friend Nobody Likes: Courtesy of being rude, overbearing and curmudgeonly; even Alastor and Rosie view her as an "ornery old bitch". Yet, she's one of the cannibals and they stick together. She's so hated that in season 2, someone set up a "memorial" to herwishingshe had died in the battle at the Hotel, despite her having survived. Fur and Loathing: She wears a fox skin with one eye crossed out draped over her shoulders, adding cruelty to animals to the list of reasons not to like her. The Heckler: The reason Susan is so tough to convince, unlike the rest of the Cannibals, is that she's a crotchety old woman who enjoys making fun of and slinging insults at people as they try to speak.

All There in the Script: Their names are revealed in theclosed captionsduring the episode which properly introduces them. Ambiguous Situation: They’re Carmilla’s daughters but whether they were a family while alive and reunited in Hell or were adopted by her in the afterlife is unclear. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Clara dresses a bit more revealingly compared to Odette.

characters.name: Mimzy
characters.description: An old friend of Alastor's when he was alive. Takes refuge in the Hotel when she's being pursued by loan sharks. '20s Bob Haircut: Mimzy has this as someone from the 20s. Acrofatic: Mimzy is overweight (and is practically the only character on the show who isn't anoodle person), but she's also known to be a talented dancer, even busting out some moves of her own at the end of the "Hell's Greatest Dad" musical number. Adapted Out: In the one-night Broadway show, she doesn't appear at the end of "Hell's Greatest Dad" and is replaced byMoxxie. All There in the Manual: The playbill reveals that Mimzy owns a club called "Ragtime" and once did a radio show with Alastor titled "Singa for ya Dinna!".

characters.name: Sheep Sinner
characters.description: A Sinner that Alastor rescues from an unpleasant fate inA Day in the After Life. Ambiguous Innocence: How she got condemned to Hell isn't easy to assume, given she exhibits no malicious tendencies whatsoever. Given Sir Pentious was condemned simply for being a coward, it's possible her own sins weren't too vile. Damsel in Distress: One so sympathetic that even the Radio Demon himself felt compelled to come to her rescue. Morality Pet: Alastor is unambiguously kind to her from the get-go. He holds the shop door open for her while begging her pardon, then comes to her rescue when she cries out for help, stating that anyone who would target a victim like her is too abhorrent even for him. The worst thing he does is massacre the butcher in front of her and then leave without checking if she's okay. Satellite Character: Her only purpose is to show that Alastor does in fact have a compassionate side. He was willing to lose out on a potentially decent butcher shop just to protect a total stranger from being attacked by its owner.

characters.name: The Butcher
characters.description: A butcher who runs a butcher shop that Alastor visits inA Day in the After Life. Ambiguous Situation: While it's presumed that he was about sexually assault the sheep customer when Alastor was about to leave, it can also be interpreted as himtrying to kill the sheep demon and sell her body parts. Of course, given how depraved he's set up as being, it could've easily beenboth. Asshole Victim: He meets a rather deserving fate of being consumed by Alastor right after he tries to assault a sheep demon. Dirty Coward: He's very much frightened ofAlastorlike every other ordinary sinner despite the fact he's willing to intimidate other patrons in his shop like the guy he just dropped or the sheep lady he was about to assault, even within the Radio Demon's presence. Even before he tried to rape the sheep lady, it was implied he planned to kill Alastor with a cleaver he was about to grab before he was intimidated by the Overlord himself. Hate Sink: With Alastor, a ruthless, cannibalistic overlord feared by all of Hell, as the comic's protagonist, it only makes sense that the Butcher is made far more loathsome by comparison so that we'll root for Al when he kills him.

characters.name: Man Meat
characters.description: A reptilian Sinner who is a colleague of Zeezi and frequents her club. Ambiguous Situation: That he's always hanging out and gossiping with Overlords would imply he is one himself, though it hasn't been confirmed and he's absent from most of their gatherings. Bad Guys Play Pool: He's seen playing pool at Klub Kaiju when he overhears Zeezi talking about the news of Alastor's defeat. Early-Bird Cameo: Appears in the pilot alongside a proto-Zeezi, having a single but lengthy line of dialogue writing off Charlie as "nuts", before returning in "Silenced" with his design virtually unchanged. Also an early cameo for Iglehart as a Hellaverse cast member, who would also portrayVortex, Asmodeus,and Zestial before reprising this role. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: His reaction to Charlie announcing her hotel to rehabilitate Sinners is to laugh and tell his friends that she's "nuts".

characters.name: Fat Nuggets
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Angel calls him "Baby Nuggs" sometimes. Ascended Extra: Only makes a couple of appearances in Season 1. In Season 2 he's significantly more prominent. Extreme Omnivore: If Angel doesn't keep him properly fed he'll start going after anything he can. In the season two opener he eats all of the bar snacks Husk put out, and by the sixth episode is outright destroying rooms and eating furniture due to being ignored and unfed. Housepet Pig: A little demon pig that Angel Dust owns and adores. Morality Pet: To Angel Dust. Fat Nuggets is the sole creature that Angel can be his most vulnerable with. He’s also the only living thing we see Angel be soft with. Bizarrely, theCountdown to Premierereveals Nuggets was a present fromValentinoof all beings. Angel outright tells Husk to watch his language around Fat Nuggets, to Husk's confusion.It's a sign that Angel is truly in a bad place when he leaves Fat Nuggets at the hotel at the end of season 2, retreating completely to his abusive life out of fear he may hurt those he loves.

characters.name: KeeKee
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Personification: According to Vivienne Medrano,KeeKeeis a living manifestation of the Hazbin Hotel itself. This is hinted at the end of "The Show Must Go On", where her eye can be seen opening at the top of the newly restored Hotel. Character in the Logo: She appears in the logo of the series as the literal iconic key that replaces the "t" in "Hotel". Cute Kitten:KeeKeehas the appearance of an incredibly cute kitty. Cuteness Overload: Has this effect on Sir Pentious and Lucifer, who start petting her on approach. Cyclops:KeeKeeis always one-eyed regardless of the form she takes.

characters.name: Alastor's Minions
characters.description: Even Evil Has Standards: Even they're weirded out by Angel's aggressive flirtations. Living Shadow: They're formed from darkness. Our Imps Are Different: They're diminutive horned monsters with mischievous expressions, though they're distinctly not imps by way ofHelluva Bosshaving already established imps as a completely different species created by Satan himself. Given Alastor desires to be Hell's most feared name, it's not surprising he'd imitate Satan in this regard. Zerg Rush: Alastor sends them to attack en masse. As his opponents included Adam and Vox at his peak, their effectiveness is pretty weak.

characters.name: Egg Boiz
characters.description: Adorable Evil Minions: Humpty-Dumpty like minions who are far more adorable than intimidating. Ambiguously Gay: The Egg Boiz all seem to have a thing for their boss, Sir Pentious. In the pilot,one of them tries to grab Sir Pentious' buttand another one even says "I wish he'd shoot ME with his ray gun." Additionally,right at the beginning of Sir Pentious' introduction, two Egg Boiz can be seen making out with each other. Artificial Human: The Egg Boiz were artificially created by Baxter when he and Sir Pentious were partners. Sir Pentious took them in and ended the partnership with Baxter when he killed one in an experiment. Beneath Notice: Frank is apparently this, as Alastor and Zestial don't even notice he accidentally boarded the elevator with them and only Rosie reacts to his being at the Overlords' meeting at all. Alastor catches on and uses this to have him act as a spy. Butt-Monkey: They are constantly cracked in their battles,and most of them die ingloriously alongside Pentious when Adam vaporizes their blimp. They don't even get to ascend to Heaven like their boss.

While Alastor has his moments of rudeness and he's a regularDeadpan Snarker, he's generally a polite and courteousSouthern Gentleman. It doesn't make him any less evil, and in fact the seeming harmlessness of his friendly exterior is a tool that he obviously uses to manipulate people like Charlie into furthering his own goals. Contrary to the main series, this is played straight in the original pilot, as he is shown to be genuinely jovial and friendly despite his sadistic desire to watch sinnersfailat redemption. Agent Peacock: He has a certain level of campiness to his character and, to quote Angel Dust, "looks like a strawberry pimp". He's also one of the strongest Sinners in Hell's history, and due to Lucifer's absence and the royals seen inHelluva Bossbeing busy with their own drama, he's currently one of the top dogs in the whole Pride Ring. characters.name: Niffty
characters.description: Clickhereto see her describe herself. Abhorrent Admirer: To Valentino after their first encounter. He considers her a freaky little annoyance, especially after stabbing him multiple times during their fight, and would have killed her (presumably), had Alastor not offered himself up to Vox in exchange for letting her and Husk go free. Accidental Hero:She deals the killing blows to Adam in the final battle, and all she was doing was stabbing any angel she could find (whose names weren't Vaggi or Angel Dust). One could say that she might betoo unhingedto be properly evil. Affectionate Nickname: Husk and Angel call her "Niff."

characters.name: Angel Dust
characters.description: Abusive Parents: It's suggested by Vox in "Hazbin Hotel: Closed Doors" that Angel's father may have hit him when they were still alive.He also guesses that him being abusive was the reason why Angel killed him, but Angel has neither the ability nor the desire to speak more on the matter. Accent Relapse: Played for horror and drama in "Masquerade", where Angel's somewhat nasally Brooklyn accent gives way to a deeper Italian accent when Valentino gives him aBreaking Speech. It's implied that this is Angel'struevoice, which further emphasizes how scared and broken he is by Valentino's abuse. Accidental Suicide: In life, Angel Dust was an addict who overdosed on the drug he's named for in 1947, resulting in his death. In Hell, he continues to do drugs, though he can't die from them due to being a sinner demon and sinners are immortal. Addled Addict: Zig-zagged. Angel is effectively immune to the physical effects of the laundry list of drugs he frequently consumes due to being a Sinner, but he still garners a lot of psychological repercussions from them. He also died of an overdose, suggesting he had serious drug problems when he was alive which ultimately killed him. Aesop Amnesia: While he does have someCharacter Developmentover the course of season 1 and is willing to become a better person,upon finding out that he's beenThe Molefor the Vees for a very long time and is forced to go against his friends, he decides that he is unworthy of redemption and goes back to his old life.Justifiedin that he only reaches that point after being thoroughlybroken, believinghe's never truly had a choice in his life since selling his soul and hating himself more than ever for both being forced to spy on the people he cares forandnearly strangling Cherri to death while under the Vees' control, fearing for their safety just as much as loathing himself and wanting them to just forget about him. Early-Bird Cameo: Prior to his proper introduction, Angel Dust can be seen among the falling si

characters.name: Cherri Bomb
characters.description: 11th-Hour Ranger: Near the end of season 1, when Heaven's army of Exorcists are on the verge of launching a premature attack on the Hazbin, Cherri joins the staff in defending the place. Rather than any change of heart on the redemption matter, her reasons to fight on their side are pairing up with her comrade-in-arms Angel and slaughter some angels come death or victory, consequences be damned.Her presence still proves to be critical: she inspires a lovelorn Pentious to make aHeroic Sacrifice, which in turn causes Charlie to unleash her fullOne-Winged Angelform and turn the tides in the battle. Action Girl: She loves blowing things up and is always ready for a good fight, and has the prowess and skills to match. Affectionate Nickname: Angel calls her "Sugar Tits" and "baby". Age-Gap Romance: Cherri, a young woman who died in her 20s, has a tentative romantic relationship with Pentious, who died in his 40s. This extends to their timeframes, as Cherri lived in Australia during the 1980s while Pentious lived in Victorian England during the 1880s, marking the difference of a century between them. Aloof Ally: Despite having fought side-by-side with the hotel residents against the Exorcists, helping rebuild it after the battle, and currently residing there, Cherri insists she'shangingat the Hazbin Hotel, notstayingthere and doesn't seem very invested in the idea of redemption. At the end of "Hazbin Hotel: Behind Closed Doors",after finding out Pentious was redeemedand realizing how empty Hell is without him, she reconsiders the idea of redemption and formally books a room at the Hotel.

characters.name: Baxter
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He created the Egg Boiz but saw nothing wrong with performing lethal experiments on them, causing Pentious to dissolve their friendship and working relationship, taking the eggs with him. Ambiguously Bi: Baxter is quick to shut down any speculation that he and Pentious were ever sexually intimate and he's shown to be quite fond of Niffty (though whether that's attraction or not is debatable). When Baxter was included in Pride merch for 2026 he was shown wearing nondescript rainbow colors as opposed to the specific colors brandished by the other characters. As the heterosexual Niffty is shown wearing black and white, it seems Baxter does identify as queer, though his exact orientation has yet to be detailed. Animal Gender-Bender: He has a lure growing from his forehead. A trait that is exclusive to female anglerfish. Granted, a sinner's form in hell is based on their perceptions so it's possible he's ignorant of this fact. Animal Motifs: Marine life, his Sinner form having an anglerfish-like head, a living bag with crustacean features, and having been the one to create Shock.wav. Because You Were Nice to Me: He is initially catty and snippy towards the Hotel and proclaims himself as aCard-Carrying Villain, consistently criticizing its goals in redemption. However,he's one of the many guests to stay at the Hotel the longest and aids them in foiling Vox's plan to invade Heaven.All for the hotel preparing his blankets at his "requested 45-degree angle to make it more tuckable to [his] liking", even hinting that it's because of Niffty.

characters.name: Rooster
characters.description: Animal Motifs: In the hotel'sDarkest Hour, Roosterchickenedout. Bird People: He is a bird-shaped humanoid, which notably contrasts with the humanoid-shaped bird appearances of the avian Goetia fromHelluva Boss. Broken Tears: After Husk insults him in the therapy session, he is left in tears. Early-Bird Cameo: Two of them.His first appearance was in the pilot, while Charlie was singing "Inside of Every Demon is a Rainbow".He subsequently appears in Episode 2 of the first season, screaming into a camera in the Doomsday District because the Extermination timetable has been cut in half. His first appearance was in the pilot, while Charlie was singing "Inside of Every Demon is a Rainbow".

characters.name: Niffty Fangirl
characters.description: Hero-Worshipper: She's a huge fan of Nifftyfor being the "Adam Slayer"to the point that she asks Niffty tostab her, wants someone to take a picture of her doing it, and cheers when Niffty obliges. Hidden Depths: Despite only coming to the Hotel to kill angels and complaining that "redemption sounds like work" after Charlie explained the Hotel's true purpose, she actually stays at the Hotel despite it not living up to her expectations.It isn't until deep into Vox's smear campaign that she finally leaves. Lazy Bum: Initially, she's not interested in redemption because she thinks it would be too much work. Major Injury Underreaction: She excitedly asks Niffty to stab her and when Niffty responds by knifing her in the gut, her only reaction is to give a pained cheer. In fairness, given she isn’t using an angelic-steel blade, the damage is likely not a big deal.Niffty Fangirl: Yessssssss... Plant Person: She's a living tree with her hair made of leaves and fruit growing out of it, and two fruits on the sides of her head that look like big earrings.

characters.name: Ant Sinner
characters.description: Accidental Pervert: His first appearance has him tripping over luggage and bracing his fall by grabbing Angel's"chest fluff". Angel accuses him of being a perv, knocks him down and then Cherri kicks him hard enough to send him flying offscreen. Butt-Monkey: He's first seen tripping over a suitcase onto Angel Dust who mistakes him for a pervert and pushes him on the ground, then he's sent flying with a kick by Cherri. Minutes later an angry Husk knocks him down and throws a bottle at him just because he asked for a Mai Tai and Husk doesn't know how to make one. Episode 3 shows Niffty hitting him with a flyswatter like he's any other pest. Early-Bird Cameo: He can be seen in the pilot listening to Charlie's pitch for the Hazbin Hotel at Klub Kaiju. No Name Given: He's not given a name at any point. Recurring Extra: He has no lines, no name and no plot importance. He's just a background character to show the Hotel has managed to get a few new guests.

characters.name: Velvette
characters.description: Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: Because of the fact that she's a doll-demon, she has the joints but none of the other restrictions. As such, she can easily twist and bend her body parts in unusual ways.During "Respectless" when she sings "You've got it twisted," she spins her head around in a full circle.AFreeze-Frame Bonusduring "Hazbin Hotel: Behind Closed Doors" has her twisting her head again like an owl as she was sitting upside down.The most prominent one was during "Scream Rain" where when Vox was berating her, she spins her head in a full circle in perfect detail for the audience to see clearly, all with aDeath Glare. During "Respectless" when she sings "You've got it twisted," she spins her head around in a full circle. AFreeze-Frame Bonusduring "Hazbin Hotel: Behind Closed Doors" has her twisting her head again like an owl as she was sitting upside down. The most prominent one was during "Scream Rain" where when Vox was berating her, she spins her head in a full circle in perfect detail for the audience to see clearly, all with aDeath Glare. Action Fashionista: She's proven to be quite a capableDark Action Girlduring "It's A Deal", while still looking pretty stylish and keeping her appearance up. In fact, what causes her to go on a murderous rampage is Husk accidentallyruining her hair.

characters.name: Ethan
characters.description: All There in the Script: His name isn't spoken in the show itself, but it's given on theVoxTek Employee Huband someofficial postsfromSpindleHorse Toons. Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: Ethan appears to be based on an electric eel, a more than appropriate complement to his boss's own theme as an electronic TV shark demon. Beleaguered Assistant: Part of Ethan's job involves fulfilling all of Vox's demands for new products, no matter how random or impractical to make they might be. Neither Velvette nor Valentino respects him very much either, laughing at his misfortune during Val's art vlog after finding out he got hit by a car, and Val punching him just because he disliked the look of Vox's super weapon. They also remark that him being allowed outside of V Tower is a rare occurrence, implying he's overworked as well. Butt-Monkey: As outlined inBeleaguered Assistantabove, he has little purpose other than to serve as a punching bag for the Vees. Fish People: He's a sinner who resembles a humanoid eel, with rubbery turquoise skin and a long piscine tail.

characters.name: Katie Killjoy
characters.description: A pompous, callous newscaster who ridicules Charlie's goals and treats everyone like garbage, even her own co-anchor. Abhorrent Admirer: Though Katie is an attractive woman, her extremely abrasive, lecherous, and off-putting personality causes Vox to completely reject her advances towards him. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She calls Adam a "fuckable bad boy" while coveringhis deathon the news. She's also willing to flirt and have sex with Vox, who's the channel's boss and main sponsor, much to his disgust. Animal Motifs: An insect of some sort as seen in herOne-Winged Angelform. Judging by the buzzing noise that sometimes accompanies her speech, it may be cicadas. Attention Whore: Big time, to the point Tom is treated more like an accessory instead of a co-host. This is how she introduces theappropriately namedKatie Killjoy Tonight:Katie: Welcome back to me...

characters.name: Tom Trench
characters.description: Katie Killjoy's co-newscaster and frequent target of her abuse. 24-Hour Armor: Tom is never seen without his gas mask on. It might be his actual face. Aerith and Bob: As the creators lampshade, the inhabitants of Hell usually have very exotic names, and then there's Tom. Ambiguously Bi: He makes a sexual comment about wanting to nail Cherri Bomb. Later, when Charlie mentions Angel Dust's name during the interview, Tomimmediatelyrecognizes that she's talking about the porn star. To this, Katie says, "You fucking would, Tom," and Tom quickly looks away, embarrassed. Butt-Monkey: Pretty much all of his appearances have him insulted, ignored, or physically abused by his co-anchor. The entire 666 News operation seems to dislike him, too, since they keep superimposing video footage and network graphics over him to block him from view. His first appearance in the pilot alone has Katie dumpingboiling hot coffee on his crotch, and it's implied this isn't the first time it's happened, not to mention that hesomehowcatches on fire once the interview devolves into an all-out brawl between Charlie and Katie.WHY WON'T ANYONE HELP MEEEEE!?!?!

characters.name: Vox's Sharks
characters.description: Black and Blue and Scary All Over: Much like their master, Vox's sharks are blue and black, and have a scary appearance. No Name Given: While Shok.wav is given a name, the rest haven't been named onscreen yet, withWord of Godsaying they call Vox's sharks "the girls". Satellite Character: Unlike Shok.wav, the other sharks haven't been given any characterization outside of being Vox's pets. Threatening Shark: Two of them surrounded Vox in the background as he comes up with a plan to spy on the hotel.

characters.name: Shok.wav
characters.description: A giant shark-shaped robot created by Baxter that's kept in Vox's shark tank and serves as his attack dog. All Animals Are Dogs: Despite Shok.wav being a cyborg demon shark, he acts like aRight-Hand Attack Dogand is treated as one by Vox and others. When Shok.wav alerts Velvette to intruders, he does so by sending her a text that says, "BARK BARK BARK", his sound design is similar to a dog's bark, andAlastor refers to him as a Vox's "little doggie" while trying to avoid his attacks. All There in the Manual: It's never stated in-series, but outside material confirmed Baxter created him. Attack! Attack! Attack!: Once he's on the hunt, Shok.wav relentlessly pursues his prey, never letting up for even a moment.Alastor is forced into a constant retreat because Shok.wav gives him no breathing room to fight back. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: He's building-sized and can smash through actual buildings with ease when he goes on the offensive.

characters.name: Melissa
characters.description: One of Velvette's models. Cute Monster Girl: She's a cute sinner demon who's seen as good-looking in-universe due to being a model. Exotic Eye Designs: She has small red heart-shaped pupils inside normal-looking black irises. Expressive Hair: Her hair is arranged in a ponytail that resembles a set of monster jaws, which remain open or shut up depending on the scene (implying her hair has a conscience of its own). Morality Pet: Downplayed. Velvette is still aMean Bossat best, but the worst she's done to Melissa is to snap at her when her temper's running high before a fashion show and the insults she levels aren't at Melissa herself but at the outfits Velvette's cycling through before deciding on a good one. AFreeze-Frame Bonusfrom "When I Think About the Future" shows the two working together and, though Velvette looks bored, Melissa's expression impliesshe likes working with Velvette.

characters.name: Travis
characters.description: All Men Are Perverts: Most of his appearances involve him drooling over Angel Dust. In the premiere, he's also seen excitedly watching a bukkake show. All There in the Script: His name has yet to appear in the show itself. He was first named ina tweetbefore the pilot's release, and later in the Season 1 playbill. Ambiguously Bi: Angel briefly asks him to tell "the missus" that he said hi, meaning that he's married to a woman, but so far he's only shown any actualattractionto men. Ascended Fanboy: Travis, once a client of Angel's in the pilot, is seen to be part of Valentino's stage crew in "Masquerade".According to the Season 1 playbill, the film they're working on in the episode,The Pure Boy, is his directorial debut. Badass Longcoat: His first full-body appearance in "Spring Broken" shows him wearing what looks like a long peacoat made of black feathers, similar to the ones on his body.

characters.name: Kitty
characters.description: A female Robo-Fizz who acts as an assistant to Valentino. Bodyguarding a Badass: Valentino is a powerful Overlord who can defend himself, but he's always accompanied by hisSexbotKitty who doubles as aKiller Robotbodyguard he can sic on people when needed. Cute Machines: She's arguably falls somewhere between “traditionally cute” and “sexy”, the latter of which being arguably the reason why Val decided to get her rather than a traditional Fizz-Bot. Distaff Counterpart: She’s a female version of the usually male Robo-Fizzes. The Dragon: To Valentino. She even becomes a serious threat to Husk and Cherri Bomb when Valentino sics her on them, going intoKiller Robotmode.

characters.name: Tiffany Titfucker
characters.description: Alliterative Name: Whileit is presumably not her real birth name, she goes byTiffanyTitfucker in her professional work. Buxom Beauty Standard: Her name and Angel's gesture when talking about her make it obvious what her main appeal as a pornstar is. The Ghost: She's only mentioned in passing by both Valentino and Angel Dust, but has never explicitly appeared onscreen. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: She and Angel are spirited rivals in the cutthroat porn industry of Pentagram City, apparently often directly competing for prestige like the coveted "Sex-x-xi Award". It's also suggested that their superior Valentino actively pits them against each other, with him telling Angel via text that he gave Tiffany his dressing room and boasting that she'll sweep the awards this year because she's trying harder than him.

characters.name: Salina
characters.description: 15 Minutes of Fame: Exaggerated, as through cinematic timing of the musical montage, Salina only has about10 secondsworth of fame as a porn actress. Allegorical Character: Salina represents young women who dream of being famous, get exploited by big corporations and studios, and are thrown out like yesterday's trash when their 15 minutes of fame are over and the public loses interest in them. All There in the Manual: Her name wouldn't be revealed until long after her debut in an Instragram post from her voice actor. Animal Motifs: Her looks seem to be based on thesecretary bird, with her eyelashes closely resembling the bird’s head frond, the orange around her eyes, and her tall, slender physique. HerShameful Stripalso shows that she has birdlike talons for feet. Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: She works for the Vees (if only briefly) and the white part of her blouse is shaped like a V.

characters.name: #-C
characters.description: 0% Approval Rating: He spends all of Season 2 cultivating himself a100% Approval Ratingby manipulating Hell and slandering Charlie and Heaven, but he undoes it all in the blink of an eye. By the end of "Curtain Call", him wildly firing the Might of Lilith in an attempt to kill Alastor with no regard for the vast swathes of Pentagram City he's disintegrating, culminating in deliberately overloading the cannon which would have resulted in the destruction of most the Pride Ring tears his reputation throughout Hell to shreds, with even Valentino and Velvette turning against him to stop the weapon, costing him his entire company and rendering him aliteral talking headwhen Valentino tears it off his body. Considering he's onlyas powerful as he is popular, it's safe to say he's out of commission for good. Achilles' Heel: By far Vox's biggest weakness ishis lack of self-worth and need for external validation, most notably shown in his obsessive need for Alastor's approval, though he constantly craves the worship of others in general. Throughout Season 2, Vox makes a truly impressive amount of progress in taking over Heaven, only for all of it to go out the window once Alastor starts exploiting his insecurities. Acquired Situational Narcissism: This is a recurring weakness of his. He's already vain and self-absorbed to begin with, but the more fame and influence he acquires the worse his egotistical tendencies become. As Alastor astutely points out, his hunger for approval stems from him alack of belief in his own ideas and abilities, so nothing will ever be enough.As "Brighter" shows, while he was already power-hungry and with an ego, after the papers called him a "god of entertainment", he got even worse and began aCult of Personalitywith himself at the center.As he gains more power over Hell, his already big ego gets larger and larger to the point that he starts thinking that he can move past his partnership with Val and Velvette once he takes over Heaven. Alastor's manip

characters.name: Zestial
characters.description: 11th-Hour Ranger: While he does leave Carmilla after she sides with Vox, he does promise to come back to her when she decides to do the right thing. Sure enough,although he doesn't come back until the Might of Lilith is about to blow, he (alongside Carmilla) are the first Overlords to willingly help the heroes save the day. Affably Evil: At least to other Overlords, as he's willing to talk casually with Alastor and shares a deep bond with Carmilla. Season 2 also shows him to be far more reasonable and less power-hungry than the other Overlords. Ancient Evil: Confirmed by bonus material to have been a feared presence in Hell for an unspecified amount of centuries. In the show itself, he's considered "ancient" by Alastor, who himself has been in Hell for almost a century, and is the oldest Overlord that's still in power. Animal Motifs: Spiders, having a spider brooch, cobweb cape, and a home full of glowing green cobwebs. He can also become an actual spider himself to spy on someone else. He also shares several positive traits associated with the creatures, being anExcellent Judge of Characterand among the most patient and intelligent of the Overlords. Animorphism: He has the ability to become a fairly large spider, which he uses to perch on the wall of Carmilla's office during her chat with Vox.

characters.name: Zeezi
characters.description: All There in the Manual: In "Scrambled Eggs", her name is only revealed in the subtitles. Her next appearance in "Silenced" has Vox refer to her by name. Animal Motifs: Dinosaurs, specifically giant theropods, as they're the type of dinosaur she resembles. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Her regular attire includes a crop top, which leaves her pink stomach exposed. Bruiser with a Soft Center: It's lampshaded that, despite being a ginormous, dinosaur-based demoness, Zeezi does have a hidden "soft" side, being touched alongside the other Overlords, that Charlie Morningstar and her friends are fighting to protect Hell and lend their aid to the effort, putting aside their own personal rivalries and joining the song, "Hear My Hope". Despite that, Zeezi has immense pride in her status, as she suggested to her fellow Overlords that they would never talk about this ever again and returned to her own agenda. Card-Carrying Villain: During "Bad With Us," she notes how much fun it is to be evil Overlords all together.

characters.name: Maestro
characters.description: Animal Motifs: Deers, having a flaming deerSkull for a Head. Early-Bird Cameo: He made a couple cameos in the Pilot before his proper debut in "Scrambled Eggs"; first as a background character in the scene where Alastor comes to watch the 666 News broadcast, and then among the crowd of Overlords in the montage where Vaggie recounts Alastor's rise to power. Humble Goal: How does Vox convince him to join his cause? By promising him a place in Heaven where he can listen to his music in peace. Odd Friendship: He and Zeezi seem to be pretty good friends, enough to greet each other in person and gossip over the phone. Meanwhile, they couldn't be more different; Zeezi is a big and loud woman who runs a techno nightclub, while Maestro is a smaller and quiet man who runs an opera house. Hilariously, this also means Vox's promises to them to get them to join his cause are opposites; he offers Zeezi locations in Heaven to start new clubs, while he offers Maestro peace and quiet. Skull for a Head: His most unique physical feature is having a deer skull for a head wreathed in blue flames.

characters.name: Prick and Hatchet
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Both characters had previously appeared in the Pilot and Season 1 exclusively as background extras, with no speaking roles aside from their brief confrontation in "Scrambled Eggs". Season 2 confirms they are Overlords, even if less influential ones compared to Alastor or the Vees. Blood Knight: Vox manages to convince them to join his cause simply with promises of giving them access to Heavenly weapons, which would allow their fights to geta lot deadlier. Bring It: Prick yells this to Hatchet in the middle of their gang war shown in "Scrambled Eggs".Hatchet:I can go all night long, baby!Prick:Bring it on, bitch! Cactus Person: Prick is a cactus demon, likely based on a Saguaro with a prickly green body and a white flower serving as his head. Cowboy: Prick styles himself in this manner, wearing typical fashion fromThe Wild West(which would also make him anOutlawby nature). He is implied to be aBounty Hunteras well, withwanted posterslittering his place.

characters.name: The Von Eldritch Family
characters.description: The Von Eldritch Family are a family of high status within Hell. Patriarch Frederick and his wife Bethesda are both Overlords, and two of the more powerful ones at that. Their daughter Helsa is a rival to Charlie Morningstar, while their son Seviathan once dated Charlie. Ambiguous Situation: We don't really have much information on the family beyond the fact that their son was once romantically involved with Charlie and that they are high enough on Hell's social ladder that they were close knit friends with the Morningstars, who sit at the very top of the food chain. Despite that, they are absent from the Overlord meetings and seem to completely uninvolve themselves in Hell's progressive social doings. Animal Motifs: Sea life, havingScary Teethsimilar to ocean predators andTentacle Hairthat evokes images of cephalopods. "Darkness von Gothick" Name: All of their names evoke central/eastern Europe, and "von Eldritch" obviously isn't a name in real life (Also,what kind of a name is "Seviathan"?). Eldritch Abomination: Their whole theme. They may not look very different from Hell's usual fare of demons, but it's implied they can shapeshift into much more grotesque forms.

characters.name: Heaven and Angels In General
characters.description: Alien Blood: Angels (as seen with both Lucifer and the Exorcists) have golden blood. Always Lawful Good: It's aZig-Zagging Tropewith Heaven, since it depends on both the angel in question and their motives at any given time.On the one hand, it's hard to deny that most of the people who wind up in Heaven are genuinely kind and decent people, or at least were at the time. This is alsodemonstratedby the overwhelming presence of many genuinely awful people going to Hell, and asHelluva Bossshows with Lyle Lipton, they do attempt to foster good behavior even in genuinely unpleasant people, meaning that the bar to entry is low and mostly boils down to having your aggregate kindness outweigh your cruelty or bad influence on other people.Season 2 reveals at least part of getting to Heaven is having in some way made up for the sins you've committed, or at least the ones that sent you to Hell in the first place (no word on sins while you were in Hell).Nowhere is this better shown than Emily, who firmly believes Sinners should be given a chance of redemption — and going by the factalmostnobodyin Heaven knew about Exterminations, the public outrage once the news broke is a sign many,manypeople object to the system and are willing to cause a reform. While it's not perfect, the system seems to mostly work to include people who are genuinely pleasant on the whole.On theotherhand, it doesn't alter the fact that just because it mostly works as intended doesn't mean the system's flaws are any less severe; the fact people likeAdamandLutehave gotten into/remain in Heaven is a sign that somereallyhorrible people can join up... or more disturbingly, that they can turn into horrible people because there's no longer any punishment for being one. Even worse,nobody in Heaven actuallyknowshow the system of salvation or damnation works until season 2 gives some clues. When Adam is put on the spot for three qualifications to ascend, and Angel Dust fails despite meeting all three of them, it just

characters.name: The Speaker of God
characters.description: Allegorical Character: The embodiment of everything that Christianity is supposed to be. She is loving, kind, patient, and forgiving. All-Loving Hero: Is nothing but kind and calm with others, from Sera to Pentious. Even when Lute, frothing with rage, is backtalking her, she remains patient, showing only calm concern for the hate erupting from one of her children. All-Powerful Bystander: She ranks above Sera, the Seraphim who rules Heaven. Accordingly, the Speaker is indicated to be insanely powerful and one of the strongest beings in all existence. She rarely involves herself in judgments or disputes, preferring to let others work things out themselves. She only makes her presence known in times of great debate, and even then, it's only to gently coax others to figure things out themselves. All There in the Manual: Prior to her debut in the show itself in "Storyteller", she got a one-off name drop in the Season 1 Playbill released in November 2024. Ambiguous Situation: As she is only referred to as the Speaker of God, and her design features scrolls as a motif, it's unknown if she is Metatron (the Angel expressly referred to as The Voice of God), or if the two are separate characters.

characters.name: Sera
characters.description: Adaptational Goal Change: Keeping the demons of Hell from uprising against Heaven was never presented as an issue for the Seraphims to deal with in most scriptures. In this series, it's the main driving force behind a majority of Sera's actions in the first season, as she's the most powerful Seraphim as well as being heavily implied to bethemost powerful Angel in all of Heaven. Affably Evil: Sera's a polite, composed angelic being who seems to feel some pity for the Sinners stuck in Hell and guilt over allowing Adam's Extermination. However, that doesn't mean she'llagree to Charlie's plan to allow redeemed Sinners to enter Heavenor call off the Exterminations, which she believes are necessary to keep Heaven safe.Subverted in Season 2 where, thanks toCharacter Development, she becomes nicer and less evil. Allegorical Character: While far from one of a bad devout religious person like Adam and Lute, Sera is one of an ignorant and misguided devout. While she acts courteous to sinners, she ultimately does not believe that they can be redeemed solely because it hasn't been proven before. And she refuses to question the system and ignorantly believes it isn't flawed despite the MANY and OBVIOUS points to the contrary.When Sir Pentious gets redeemed right in front of her, (and after a month of denial) she realizes that her enabling yearly genocide wasAll for Nothing, and that herBlack-and-White Insanityhas prevented her from understanding theHidden Depthsof others such as demons and on a larger scalehumans themselves, and being open to possible alternative solutions to improve the flaws in the system and build relationships with others who are more willing to acknowledge and fix their shared problems, due to her pride in her status and fear of hell and the damned, making her reluctant to address or effectively deal with the problems arising in hell because of her actions, causing them to fester and grow into something she and heaven can't ignore.Ironicallyher devotion and

characters.name: Emily
characters.description: The Alleged Boss: Emily, though much younger, is of equal rank as her sister, Sera. However, due to her childlike and unauthoritive personality, she comes off more like a consultant andTagalong Kidthan a fellow ruler. Emily clearly enjoys speaking to residents on peer to peer terms, even in the face of Lute's callousness, she is more liable to bicker with her like two schoolchildren. Her few acts of authority are letting Sir Pentious interact with the Council, and turning down Lute as Exorcist leader over Abel, and even this was largely more for pragmatic reasons rather than to discipline the volatile Lieutenant. Allegorical Character: In contrast to Adam, who's the distillation of a bad devout religious person, and Sera, who is one of a misguided ignorant devout, Emily is the distillation of a good and open-minded one. She's polite towards other people, humble despite her high standing, and, most important, compassionate even towards those who have sinned. And she sees the flaws in the system, is unafraid to speak up against it, and fully believes in Charlie's idea of a sinner being redeemed despite there being no proof. All-Loving Hero: Similar to Charlie, she holds great compassion for all beings, including residents of Hell. She pushes to give Angel Dust a chance when Adam and Sera say his hedonism makes him unworthy of redemption, and her entire role in Heaven is to ensure its residents are as happy and content as possible. Upon learning of the Exterminations, she immediately declares that Heaven's system is broken if it allows such atrocities to continue without those involved being cast out.Season 2 even shows she's already forgiven Sera and still loves her. Depsite Vox's taunts to her and the other angels, she still defends him when Lute gets in his face and doesn't even show any resentment to him for (accidentally but with no regret) taking out one of her wings, just concern/worry at the sight of hisVillainous Breakdown, rescues random Sinners during the ba

characters.name: Saint Peter
characters.description: Adaptational Costume Change: In many paintings and statues, Saint Peter wears a tunic with a cloak fastened at the shoulder. Here, he dons an alice blue vest over a canary yellow shirt with the long sleeves sporting reddish-gold cuffs, and a blue skirt that matches his vest with cross at the hem matching his cuffs. This is moreso a nod to how he's usually depicted wearing blue-ish clothing in paintings. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the Bible, Peter has a lot of decidedly unchristian moments, like denying Jesus three times or cutting off a Roman soldier's ear. Here he seems a lot more pleasant to be around, though it has been about 2,000 years since his death. Adaptation Dye-Job: He is often depicted in art and other media as being a brunet whenever he's shown in his younger years. Here, Peter has blonde hair. Age Lift: Most art and media depictions of Saint Peter show him as a bearded old man, whereas this series portrays him as being significantly younger and beardless. All There in the Manual: The playbill mentions that he's the lead singer in Heaven's royal choir, established their drama club and plays the harp and French horn in the "Sera-ymphany" orchestra (that's his word for it).

characters.name: Molly
characters.description: All There in the Manual: There's no indication within the show itself beyond aesthetic similarities in their design that Molly is Angel's sister since she only appears in cameo and doesn't directly speak with Charlie, but it has since been confirmed byWord of God. Animal Motifs: Spiders, her appearance having elements of one like her brother. In contrast to Angel Dust's four arms, she has four legs. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: She doesn't seem to be wearing any footwear on her four feet, leaving her claws exposed. Beauty Equals Goodness: She is a part of St. Peter's "Everyone in Heaven is Hot" lineup. Cute Monster Girl: Like her brother, her design resembles a humanoid spider, but she's fluffy and adorable with big expressive eyes.

characters.name: Adam's Apparition
characters.description: Notthat Adam. This one is a figment of Lute's imagination and fracturing psyche following the real Adam's death at Hell's hands. Ambiguous Situation: How much of Lute's hallucination is an accurate representation of Adam and how much is Lute's own idealized perception of him? Adam certainly was as vulgar and rude in life as Lute remembers him to be, and his opinion of Abel is something even Abel doesn't deny, but the care he shows for her seems more likely to be an expression of Lute's grief than his actual feelings on the matter, something the hallucination indirectly points out by acknowledging that he's no more aware of Adam's feelings than Lute herself is. Animal Motifs: His hunched over stance when egging Lute on resembles a vulture. Vultures are often held as symbols of death and rebirth, which fits this version of Adam since he's a memory brought to life. Vultures feed on the dead and Adam is gleeful at the thought of Lute committing mass murder in his name. Breaking the Fourth Wall: After calling Abel a pussy, he turns and points directly at the camera to clarify that he doesn't mean the good kind. Brutal Honesty: He'sveryforthright about being nothing but a hallucination and makes no attempt to prolong Lute's hope that the real Adam knew about her feelings for him.

characters.name: Vox
characters.description: Dark Is Evil: He has a black television-shaped head with a dark blue screen, and wears a navy blue tuxedo and a black top hat. He's also one of the major antagonists in the series and one of Hell's most powerful Overlords. Dark Messiah: Vox spends the second season building up his reputation as a savior for Sinners who will build a brighter future for them and lead them to Heaven. Not through redemption as Charlie advocates, but by slaughtering the angels that have been exterminating them for the past 7 years, ignoring their overtures of peace, and simply conquering paradise. All the while, Vox cares nothing for the lives of the followers he amasses, and merely wants everyone in Heaven and Hell to buy into his god complex and worship him unconditionally forever. Death by Irony: In life, he was a TV presenter who engineered accidents to kill his coworkers who were more popular than him. He died when a TV fell on his head as he was giving aRousing Speechto a large crowd. Death Seeker: By the end of season 2 Vox is so broken from realizing he'll never get Alastor's validation and is going to lose everything, he not only tries to detonate everyone, including himself, but he even begs the other Vees not to stop the weapon from exploding.
